prompts.zero_shot:
You are a clinical reasoning expert. Predict how key lab values evolve following a clinical management decision.

## Patient chart up to the index time
**Chief complaint:** Chest pain

**History of present illness:**
:
Mr. ___ is a ___ yo man with h/o CAD s/p PCI in ___, 
symptomatic bradycardia s/p PPM, who presents with chest pain.

Patient reported right sided chest pain at 1 pm lasting 
approximately 5 minutes. Reportedly this felt similar to a prior 
infection in the area. He had no shortness of breath of 
diaphoresis associated with this.

In the ED, initial vitals were unremarkable. Patient reported 
ongoing mild ___ chest pain. ECG showed ST depression in V1-V6. 
Labs were notable for a troponin-T of 2.49 with CK-MB of 7. CXR 
showed increased cardiomegaly and new pulmonary edema and small 
pleural effusions bilaterally. Patient was given full dose 
aspirin and started on a heparin gtt.

After arrival on the cardiology ward, the patient and his wife 
were interviewed with the assistance by telephone of a ___ 
interpreter. He endorsed sudden onset right sided chest pain 
along with dyspnea on exertion. The pain lasted "a few minutes" 
then subsided, and he noted coincident loss of appetite without 
nausea or emesis. Since, he has noted slightly worsening dyspnea 
on exertion, feeling out of breath when just walking 5 minutes. 
He also noticed feeling dizzy at times, noting his SBP in the 
100s, which he typically runs in the mid ___. Today, while at 
his PCP, he endorsed repeat right sided chest pain that was more 
intense, prompting today's visit. The pain subsided shortly 
after arriving at the emergency department. At admission, he was 
without chest pain and dyspnea. He denied orthopnea.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
Positive per HPI.
Cardiac review of systems is notable for absence of paroxysmal 
nocturnal dyspnea, orthopnea, ankle edema, palpitations, 
syncope, or presyncope.
On further review of systems, he denied fevers or chills, any 
prior history of stroke, TIA, bleeding at  …[truncated]

**Admission physical exam:**
On admission
GENERAL: Well developed, well nourished elderly East Asian man 
in NAD. Oriented x3. Mood, affect appropriate.
VS: T 97.4 BP 122/70 HR 75 RR 24 SaO2 97% on O2 2 LPM via NC
Admit wt: 66.3  kg
HEENT: Normocephalic atraumatic. Sclera anicteric. PERRL. EOMI. 
Conjunctiva were pink. No pallor or cyanosis of the oral mucosa. 
No xanthelasma.
NECK: Supple. JVP elevated to earlobe.
CARDIAC: PMI located in ___ intercostal space, midclavicular 
line. Regular rate and rhythm. Normal S1, S2. No murmurs, rubs, 
or gallops. No thrills or lifts.
LUNGS: No chest wall deformities or tenderness. Respiration 
unlabored with no accessory muscle use. Crackles throughout 
bilateral posterior lung fields up to scapula
ABDOMEN: Soft, non-tender, non-distended. No hepatomegaly. No 
splenomegaly.
EXTREMITIES: Warm, well perfused. No clubbing, cyanosis, or 
peripheral edema.
SKIN: No significant skin lesions or rashes.
PULSES: Distal pulses palpable and symmetric.

**All labs measured before the index (latest [range], n):**
- Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT): 72.0 IU/L (range 72.0–72.0, n=1)
- Albumin: 3.4 g/dL (range 3.4–3.4, n=1)
- Alkaline Phosphatase: 48.0 IU/L (range 48.0–48.0, n=1)
- Anion Gap: 17.0 mEq/L (range 17.0–17.0, n=1)
- Asparate Aminotransferase (AST): 87.0 IU/L (range 87.0–87.0, n=1)
- Bicarbonate: 21.0 mEq/L (range 21.0–21.0, n=1)
- Bilirubin, Total: 0.9 mg/dL (range 0.9–0.9, n=1)
- Calcium, Total: 8.3 mg/dL (range 8.3–8.3, n=1)
- Chloride: 104.0 mEq/L (range 104.0–104.0, n=1)
- Creatine Kinase, MB Isoenzyme: 5.0 ng/mL (range 5.0–6.0, n=2)
- Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL (range 1.0–1.0, n=1)
- Glucose: 98.0 mg/dL (range 98.0–98.0, n=1)
- H: 71.0 (range 0.0–71.0, n=2)
- Hematocrit: 36.7 % (range 36.7–36.7, n=1)
- Hemoglobin: 12.1 g/dL (range 12.1–12.1, n=1)
- I: 1.0 (range 1.0–1.0, n=2)
- L: 17.0 (range 8.0–17.0, n=2)
- Lactate Dehydrogenase (LD): 624.0 IU/L (range 624.0–624.0, n=1)
- MCH: 32.4 pg (range 32.4–32.4, n=1)
- MCHC: 33.0 g/dL (range 33.0–33.0, n=1)

- NTproBNP: 2055.0 pg/mL (range 2055.0–2055.0, n=1)
- PTT: 34.9 sec (range 34.9–52.8, n=2)
- Phosphate: 2.6 mg/dL (range 2.6–2.6, n=1)
- Platelet Count: 142.0 K/uL (range 142.0–142.0, n=1)
- Potassium: 4.4 mEq/L (range 4.4–4.4, n=1)
- RDW: 12.9 % (range 12.9–12.9, n=1)
- RDW-SD: 46.1 fL (range 46.1–46.1, n=1)
- Red Blood Cells: 3.73 m/uL (range 3.73–3.73, n=1)
- Sodium: 138.0 mEq/L (range 138.0–138.0, n=1)
- Troponin T: 2.29 ng/mL (range 2.29–2.47, n=2)
- Urea Nitrogen: 24.0 mg/dL (range 24.0–24.0, n=1)
- White Blood Cells: 6.5 K/uL (range 6.5–6.5, n=1)

## Cardiac markers to predict (pre-intervention series)
**Cardiac Markers (pre-intervention, value @ hours-before-index):**
- Troponin T: 2 measurements [2.470@12h, 2.290@5h], latest=2.290

## Clinical Management
Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) — coronary revascularization was performed.
Index time: 2190-05-01T12:00:00

## Task
For EACH lab below, predict its trajectory over the 96 hours after the index time:
  - "troponin"  (Troponin T)

Return ONLY a JSON object keyed by lab id. Each entry has a direction ("rising" | "falling" | "stable") and 4 values [at 24h, 48h, 72h, 96h].
Example format:
{"troponin": {"direction": "stable", "values": [0, 0, 0, 0]}}

Return ONLY the JSON, no other text.
